analysis.title: Marketcolour + FOMC/Budget/Earnings (Ioannis Blekos, 29 Oct 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed higher Wednesday: SPX +28bps to 7743 (8 of 11 sectors up, Tech +0.48%, Utilities -0.88%), NDX +55bps to 29813, RTY +41bps to 2830.
The Fed held rates as expected, with the funds rate unchanged at 3.75-4.00%. GS reads recent Fed comments as pointing to a compromise of hiking every other meeting.
GS expects a second and final Fed hike in December. A third hike in March is possible if inflation comes in higher than GS expects.
GS expects the ECB to deliver one more 25bp hike in December, taking the peak policy rate to 2.75%.

Wednesday was the first real day of rotation back into AI in recent weeks. Drivers were fading capital raise overhangs (META, SPCX), better tech prints overnight (SKHY, VRT) and ORCL +10%. The GS Data Center Basket (GSTMTDAT) rose 2.59%.
MSFT rose about 4% after hours after a Q3 revenue beat. ORCL rose 10% after reaffirming its positive 2027 guide at its investor day.
In Europe, UK banks (GSSBBKDU +1.8%, after the Budget), EU power names (GSXEPOWR +1.4%) and EU semis (GSSBSEMI +1.3%) outperformed.
Basket idea: GS reiterates its bullish AI view and highlights the rebalanced AI Health Care Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCAIP). The group shows low correlation to AI, the opposite of AI, rates and oil.

UK Budget broadly matched expectations. Higher debt interest costs pushed up the OBR deficit projections and reduced fiscal space. The Chancellor announced tax increases raising £6bn a year by 2029/30, temporary cost-of-living measures and funding for the Defence Investment Plan.

Airbus Q3 adjusted EBIT of €1,768mn was about 1% below consensus on revenue of €17.47bn, about 2% below. FCF before customer financing was -€102mn vs company-compiled consensus of +€325mn. Guidance of about 870 deliveries was confirmed.
On the Airbus call, management said it is comfortable at 870 plus or minus 20 deliveries. P&W engines remain the pacing item, and 2027/2028 output is not at risk.

Prysmian beat and raised. EBITDA beat by 7%, driven by a 20% beat in Electrification. Fibre and Power Grid missed. FCF was light in the quarter. The EBITDA guide midpoint rose to 3.1bn, implying about 6% upgrades to consensus.
SocGen beat and made a small raise, with mid-single-digit upgrades to 2026 consensus earnings. GS sees the stock up 2-3% but doubts it will hold.
ING missed net profit by 6%, with the miss across most lines. GS expects the stock down 3-5%.
MTU Aero Q3 EBIT was a 1% miss, with OEM weakness and strong commercial MRO. FCF of 172m beat consensus of 109m, and GS expects the FCF raise to be well received.
WPP Q3 organic net sales were -2.1%, better than the GSe/Vuma consensus of -3.3%/-3.2%. Net sales of £2,411m were about 1% above expectations. WPP Media returned to 0.3% growth from -2.8% in Q2.

GOOGL 3Q26 revenue was $127.6bn (+25% y/y), in line with consensus. Operating income of $40.6bn missed consensus of $43.4bn. Google Cloud revenue was $30.71bn (+103% y/y). GS cut its price target from $435 to $385 and kept Buy.

MSFT 1QFY revenue of $92.3bn (+19% cc y/y) was 2% above the Street. Non-GAAP EPS of $4.89 (+27% y/y) was 3% above the Street. GS says investor focus in the AI ecosystem has shifted to token demand sustainability and the depth of financing markets.

market_movers.rationale: Guidance of about 870 deliveries was confirmed and the FY26 outlook is unchanged. Q3 adjusted EBIT and revenue were slightly below consensus.
Price target cut from $435 to $385. Q3 operating income missed consensus, but GS sees Alphabet as well positioned for AI adoption.
Listed as Conviction Buy with 30% upside. Q1 FY revenue and non-GAAP EPS beat the Street.

sector_views.rationale: GS reiterates its bullish AI view. Rotation back into AI and data center names resumed after capital raise overhangs eased.

earnings_insights: GOOGL 3Q26 reported: revenue $127.6bn (+25% y/y), in line with consensus. Operating income $40.6bn reported vs consensus $43.4bn. Search & Other $63.35bn (+12% y/y), YouTube Ads $11.21bn, Google Cloud $30.71bn (+103% y/y).
MSFT 1QFY (September) reported: revenue $92.3bn (+19% cc y/y), 2% above the Street. Non-GAAP EPS $4.89 reported (+27% y/y), 3% above the Street. Shares indicated about +3% after hours.
Airbus Q3 reported: adjusted EBIT €1,768mn, about 1% below consensus. Revenue €17.47bn, about 2% below consensus. FCF before customer financing -€102mn vs company-compiled consensus of +€325mn.
Prysmian reported: EBITDA beat by 7%, Electrification beat by 20%. FY EBITDA guide midpoint raised to 3.1bn, implying about 6% upgrades to consensus.
WPP Q3 reported: organic net sales -2.1% vs GSe/Vuma consensus of -3.3%/-3.2%. Net sales £2,411m, about 1% ahead of expectations.
MTU Aero Q3 reported: EBIT a 1% miss. FCF 172m vs consensus 109m.
ING reported: net profit missed by 6%. SocGen reported: beat with a small raise, and GS sees mid-single-digit upgrades to 2026 consensus earnings.
